name: rhodium
notes: OTC quote (Johnson Matthey / LBMA).  Reference $320k/kg = $9,950/oz (May 8 2026 spot).  Trace PGM in M-type / iron-meteorite analogues.

name: iridium
notes: OTC quote.  Trace PGM in iron-meteorite analogues.

name: gold
notes: COMEX gold front-month.  Reference $150k/kg = ~$4,700/oz; gold ran from $3,335 (May 2025) to $4,732 (May 2026) per Reuters analyst consensus.

name: platinum
notes: NYMEX platinum front-month.  Reference $45k/kg = $1,400/oz, mid of Heraeus 2026 forecast $1,300-$1,800/oz.

name: palladium
notes: NYMEX palladium front-month.  Reference $48k/kg = $1,495/oz spot (May 2026, LBMA via lppm.com).

name: water
notes: Price depends entirely on where the water is SOLD, not on the asteroid — see DELIVERY_DESTINATIONS. Set MINERAL_CONFIG.delivery_destination to 'leo' or 'cislunar' to price it as launch cost avoided; the default 'earth_surface' prices it as what it is once landed, which is bulk industrial water.

name: cobalt
notes: LME cobalt cash; trace constituent of FeNi alloys.

name: nickel
notes: LME 3-month nickel.

name: copper
notes: COMEX copper front-month.

name: iron
notes: Priced as refined steel scrap (Q1 2026 mid-range $343/MT US, $400/MT global — $0.34-0.50/kg).  Asteroid mining produces refined iron from nickel-iron alloy, NOT iron ore — so the relevant sale price is steel scrap / refined metal, not the $0.10/kg iron-ore benchmark.

name: chromium
notes: Aluminothermic chromium metal, ~$10-12/kg (USGS MCS 2025 carries ferrochrome and metal).  Stainless alloying.

name: titanium
notes: Titanium sponge, ~$7-10/kg (USGS MCS 2025 import unit value).  Structural.

name: ammonia
notes: Anhydrous ammonia, US Gulf ~$450/t in 2024 (USGS MCS 2025 nitrogen).  Solid density.  In space: nitrogen for atmospheres, fertiliser, and resistojet propellant.

name: carbon dioxide
notes: Industrial liquid CO2, ~$50-150/t; not a USGS commodity.  Solid density.  In space: the carbon feed for Sabatier methane and a life-support buffer gas.

name: sulfur
notes: USGS MCS 2025 elemental sulfur, ~$80-100/t in 2024.  In space: sulfur concrete binder and sulfuric-acid leachant.

name: phosphorus
notes: Elemental (P4) trade price, ~$3,000/t; USGS lists phosphate rock, not the element.  In space: fertiliser for agriculture.

name: silver
notes: COMEX silver front-month.

name: ruthenium
notes: OTC quote.  Trace PGM.

name: osmium
notes: Specialty quote; very illiquid.

name: gallium
notes: High-purity gallium, 2024 ~$500-700/kg after China's export controls (USGS MCS 2025).  Iron meteorites carry 2-100 ppm.

name: germanium
notes: Zone-refined germanium, 2024 ~$2,000-3,000/kg (USGS MCS 2025).  Siderophile: iron meteorites carry 0.1-500 ppm.

name: rhenium
notes: Rhenium metal pellets, 2024 ~$1,200-1,600/kg (USGS MCS 2025).  Highly siderophile, tracks osmium in meteoritic metal.

name: tungsten
notes: APT ~$340/mtu in 2024 (USGS MCS 2025) = ~$43/kg of contained W (1 mtu = 10 kg WO3 = 7.93 kg W).

name: molybdenum
notes: Molybdic oxide ~$20/lb of contained Mo in 2024 (USGS MCS 2025) = ~$44/kg.

name: nickel-iron
notes: Iron-meteorite analogue (IIIAB octahedrite mean) — Fe + Ni + trace PGMs + Au.  Total PGM ≈ 37 ppm matches siderite literature.  Yields cover all 6 PGMs as of v1.1.2.

name: awaruite
notes: Ni-rich Fe-Ni alloy (Ni 75.9 wt%, Fe 24.1 wt%) with concentrated PGMs (5× nickel-iron baseline).  Terrestrial analog: Josephine / Mojave ophiolites.  Documented in some ureilites and rare meteoritic phases.  Use as a high-grade target where spectral data suggests PGM enrichment beyond bulk Fe-Ni.

name: schreibersite
notes: Fe-Ni phosphide, 1.5-3% of iron-meteorite and enstatite-chondrite metal.  The phosphorus source in an asteroid.

name: carbon
notes: Amorphous / graphitic carbon (not gem diamond).

name: magnetite
notes: Iron-oxide ore; priced as Fe content.

name: chromite
notes: Cr-Fe spinel oxide; ~0.5 wt% of ordinary chondrites, ~1% of HEDs.

name: ilmenite
notes: Fe-Ti oxide; ~1 wt% of eucrites.  The same mineral lunar ISRU plans reduce for oxygen.

name: troilite
notes: Iron sulfide, standing for all Fe sulfides (troilite, pyrrhotite).  Yields Fe and S.

name: spinel
notes: Mg-Al oxide; high-T refractory.

name: plagioclase
notes: Feldspar group; basaltic-crust marker.

name: oxides
notes: Generic metal-oxide bulk.

name: olivine
notes: Mg-Fe silicate.  Fa10 mean; bulk industrial use only.

name: pyroxene
notes: Mg-Fe-Ca chain silicate.

name: orthopyroxene
notes: Mg-Fe end of the pyroxene series.

name: enstatite
notes: Mg-pyroxene end-member; E-chondrite analogue.

name: phyllosilicates
notes: Hydrated clays, priced as dehydrated rock: their bound water is the catalog's ice fraction.

name: silicates
notes: Catch-all rock-forming silicate bulk.

name: carbonates
notes: Calcite, dolomite, breunnerite: 2-5 wt% of CI chondrites.  Calcining releases the CO2.

name: organics
notes: Complex organic macromolecules (kerogen-like).

name: sperrylite
notes: Pt arsenide (Pt 56.6 wt%) — dominant terrestrial Pt ore.  Documented in some iron meteorites and in Sudbury impact-melt-class material.  Arsenic is toxic but recoverable; ignored in valuation.

name: laurite
notes: Ru sulfide (Ru 61.2 wt%) with trace Ir / Os substitution.  Found in PGM-bearing chromites and rare iron-meteorite phases.

name: native-pgm
notes: Mixed native PGM alloy (Pt 70 wt%, Pd 15, Ir 8, Os 5, Ru 1, Rh 1).  Implied value ≈ $55k/kg — by far the richest mineral phase in the catalog.  Extremely rare; documented as nuggets in some ureilites, rare iron meteorites, and Os-Ir-Ru alloys.  Reserved for high-confidence per-asteroid override use cases.
